# MacLayout

> MacLayout is a macOS menu bar app that saves, restores, and automates window layouts. It captures the position and size of every open window across multiple monitors and restores them with a single click, keyboard shortcut, or automated trigger. Unlike simple window snapping tools (Rectangle, Magnet), MacLayout saves *complete named layouts* and can auto-trigger them when displays change or apps launch.

## Key Information

- **Category**: macOS Utility / Window Manager / Productivity
- **Platform**: macOS 13 (Ventura) or later, Intel and Apple Silicon
- **Pricing**: $19.99 one-time purchase, 14-day free trial
- **Developer**: Daniel White (Sweden)
- **Website**: https://maclayout.com

## Core Features

- Save unlimited named window layouts (e.g., "Home Office", "Focus Mode", "Presentation")
- Restore layouts with one click from the menu bar or global keyboard shortcuts
- Multi-monitor support with smart relative positioning when displays change
- Auto-trigger layouts on display configuration change (dock/undock laptop)
- Auto-trigger layouts on app launch (e.g., open Slack → communication layout)
- macOS Spaces support
- Lightweight menu bar app — no Dock clutter

## Key Differentiators vs Competitors

| Feature | MacLayout | Rectangle | Magnet | Moom |
|---------|-----------|-----------|--------|------|
| Save named layouts | Yes | No | No | Yes |
| Auto-trigger on display change | Yes | No | No | No |
| Auto-trigger on app launch | Yes | No | No | No |
| macOS Spaces support | Full | Partial | Partial | Partial |
| Smart relative positioning | Yes | No | No | Partial |
| Price | $19.99 | Free/$9.99 | $7.99 | $15 |

## FAQ

- **Why Accessibility permission?** MacLayout uses macOS Accessibility APIs to read and control window positions. It never accesses personal data or tracks activity.
- **Works with multiple monitors?** Yes, with smart positioning that adapts layouts when display configuration changes.
- **Subscription?** No. One-time purchase with 1 year of updates included.
- **Why not on the Mac App Store?** App Store sandboxing prevents access to the Accessibility APIs needed for window management.
- **System requirements?** macOS 13 (Ventura) or later, Intel or Apple Silicon.
